newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche to take over Tastemaker.
newsitem.headline: Roche to take over Tastemaker.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals concern Roche Holding AG said it would take over U.S. food and beverage flavours concern Tastemaker.

"Roche will take over Tastemaker. On February 4, Roche signed an agreement with Hercules Inc and Mallinckrodt Group Inc, both based in the U.S., which both hold 50 percent of the shares of Tastemaker," Roche said in a statement.
Roche did not disclose the purhcase price.
Tastemaker manufactures and sells flavour compounds, citrus specialties and process flavours for the food and beverage industry. Its 1996 sales were about $320 million, Roche said.
Tastemaker is based in Cincinnati, Ohio, with operations in Holland, England, Mexico, Australia and Japan.
The acquisition will "be an excellent strategic fit and will ideally complement the activities of Givaudan-Roure, Roche's fragrances and flavours division," Roche said.
Givaudan-Roure is part of the Roche group and an international company in the fragrances, flavours and aroma chemicals business. Its consolidated sales in 1996 totaled 1.4 billion Swiss francs.
The acquisition is in line with Roche's goal of further strengthening its four core businesses: pharmaceuticals, vitamins and fine chemicals, diagnostics, and fragrances and flavours, Roche said.
